CITY OF SAN JOSE -- MEMORANDUM
JOHN HAMILTON, DIRECTOR OF PLANNING
ATTN: HUGH BAKER
SUBJECT CDBG - DRAFT EIR
FROM
GENE SAALWAECHTER, DIRECTO
PARKS AND RECREATION
MARCH 10, 1978
.. ニント・ にいい
APPROVED
DATE
Submitted herewith are our comments on the Draft Environmental Impact Report for the :: Community Development Block Grant Three-Year Plan, July 1978 - June 1981 (PP 78-10):
General Comments
70
The Draft EIR, and particularly the Summary, should distinguish between proposed and potential mitigation measures as per California Environmental Quality Act requirements. As it appears, the listed mitigation measures are suggested actions which have not been incorporated in the projects' design at this time.
Specific Comments
1. Page 8. Second paragraph under Backesto Park discussion to read: "THIS PROJECT WILL ALSO PROVIDE $11,000 FOR construction of a PAR physical fitness course." 
2. Page 66. First sentence under discussion of neighborhood parks to read:
3. Page 83. Discussion of Alma Neighborhood Center under Public Facilities.

The conclusion that the ground failure potential does not warrant a negative impact appears to conflict with the conclusion on page 101 that the liquefaction potential at this site constitutes an unavoidable adverse impact.
4. Page 86. First sentence under Community Facilities to read: "The RECOM-MENDED improvements to Backesto Park include the construction of a shelter-type recreation building, SUBJECT TO CITIZEN APPROVAL IN THE PARK MASTER PLANNING PROCESS."
5. Page 87. Delete third sentence of last paragraph. No EIR has been prepared on the development of Plata Arroyo Park.
6: Page 88. Discussion under Alma CNRA to read: "The Alma Neighborhood in Center is the only project which could impact trees, and this structure is SHOULD be sited to preserve specimen trees."
7. Pages 105-106. Delete last two paragraphs on page 105 (commencing with "A comprehensive park...") and the first four sentences on page 106 (concluding with "...the proposed plan."). This discussion draws spurious conclusions related to the potential impacts of park development which vary with park size, location, community attitudes and a variety of other factors.
You have any questions, please contact Martin Sawa at extension 4571.
GENE SAALWAECHTER, DIRECTOR
PARKS AND RECREATION
